# CONF-008: Unknown tools get a JSON-RPC error, not a tool result

| Severity | Applies to | Spec section |
|---|---|---|
| info | both eras, stdio, http | [2026-07-28/server/tools#error-handling](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#error-handling) |

Calls a tool name that is not in tools/list (checked first, so no real tool is ever called). The spec's error-handling section lists an unknown tool as a protocol error, returned as a standard JSON-RPC error, as opposed to tool execution errors reported with isError: true. The section has no MUST or SHOULD, so this is info and never fails a run. Any JSON-RPC error code passes; the spec's example uses -32602. The 2025-11-25 tools page lists unknown tools as a protocol error too. On servers that speak both eras it runs twice: once with modern requests, and once inside a legacy initialize session as <ID>@legacy.

From the command line: `mcpprobe checks explain CONF-008`. To leave it out of a run, add `"CONF-008"` to `[checks] disable` in [mcpprobe.toml](../configuration.md); to change how much it counts, use `severity_overrides`.
